templates.template_en: The '{construct}' construct is not allowed at this language level.

ar.template: البنية «{construct}» غير مسموح بها في هذا المستوى من اللغة.

review_flags: Impersonal passive agreement: confirm 'غير مسموح بها' (masculine participle + feminine pronoun referring to البنية) is the preferred MSA form over fully agreeing 'غير مسموحة'.
Terminology: 'البنية' chosen for 'construct' (AST/grammar structure); reviewer confirm vs alternatives 'التركيب' or 'الصيغة' for young learners.

Agreement anchor: adjectives agree with the head noun البنية, never with the interpolated value — confirm this reads naturally whether {construct} renders as an English AST name (ClassDeclaration) or a localized label.
Quote style: straight ASCII quotes around a Latin identifier inside RTL text — confirm acceptable given render-time bidi isolation (stored template is clean by policy).

templates.template_en: The '{construct}' construct is intentionally excluded from this language level.

review_flags: Intent nuance: 'عن قصد' chosen over 'عمدا' to avoid the legal/punitive connotation of premeditation; confirm it conveys a deliberate design choice (not a bug, not a punishment) warmly enough for young learners.

Double preposition: 'مستبعدة عن قصد من هذا المستوى من اللغة' repeats من (excluded FROM + level OF the language) — confirm fluency; if clunky, reviewer may prefer restructuring, but keep the shared cluster frame.
Gender agreement: 'مستبعدة' agrees with feminine البنية — confirm.
Quote style: straight ASCII quotes around a Latin identifier inside RTL text — confirm acceptable given render-time bidi isolation.

templates.template_en: '{global}' is not available at this language level.

ar.template: الاسم «{global}» غير متاح في هذا المستوى من اللغة.

review_flags: Added head noun: Arabic inserts 'الاسم' (absent from the English) to anchor gender agreement and avoid an adjective directly modifying a foreign token — confirm 'الاسم' is the right classifier for globals like Math/console; alternative: 'المعرف'.

Agreement anchor: 'غير متاح' (masc) tracks الاسم regardless of interpolation — confirm it still reads correctly if {global} renders as an Arabic pack word of different apparent gender (e.g. رياضيات for Math), where the quoted token is an apposition/name.

Register: confirm 'غير متاح' carries the intended 'not unlocked yet at this level' (availability) reading rather than a permanent absence, matching the pedagogical gradient vs the not-allowed and intentionally-excluded keys.
Quote style: straight ASCII quotes around a Latin identifier inside RTL text — confirm acceptable given render-time bidi isolation.

templates.template_en: The member '{member}' is not available at this language level.

review_flags: Terminology: 'العضو' is the standard Arabic OOP term for member, but its everyday senses (limb, organization member) may read oddly for children; reviewer weigh alternatives 'الخاصية' (property) / 'الدالة' (method) — note the JEJ member surface spans BOTH properties (length) and methods (split, floor), so any replacement must cover both.
Agreement anchor: 'غير متاح' (masc) tracks العضو, not the interpolated value — confirm it holds when {member} renders as an Arabic pack word (e.g. طول for length, أرضية for floor).
Register: confirm the availability reading ('not unlocked at this level') as in jej.global_not_available.
Quote style: straight ASCII quotes around a Latin identifier inside RTL text — confirm acceptable given render-time bidi isolation.

templates.template_en: The logical operator '{operator}' is not allowed at this language level.

templates.template_en: The body of '{construct}' must be wrapped in curly braces {{ }}.

ar.template: يجب وضع جسم «{construct}» بين قوسين معقوصين {{ }}.

review_flags: Bracket terminology: chose 'قوسين معقوصين' for { }; naming varies regionally (معقوف vs معقوص vs حاصرة) — confirm the clearest term for young learners; the literal {{ }} symbols anchor the meaning regardless of term choice.

Interpolation agreement: {construct} is a quoted code token in apposition to 'جسم', so no gender/case agreement is structurally required — verify it still reads naturally with real pack values (e.g. 'إذا', 'طالما') and with Latin-script fallback tokens.

RTL rendering check: stored template keeps the escaped literal braces {{ }} and ASCII quotes adjacent to RTL text with no bidi controls (per ratified policy — isolation is applied at render time); reviewer should eyeball the rendered message to confirm the brace pair and quoted token appear in the correct visual order.
Term 'جسم' (body) is the standard Arabic CS term (جسم الدالة/الحلقة); confirm age-appropriateness for absolute beginners vs a more transparent alternative like 'محتوى'.
ASCII quotes '…' around {construct} kept for catalog-wide consistency with code-token display; reviewer may prefer Arabic guillemets «…» — decide once for the whole catalog, not per message.

templates.template_en: You can only assign to variables — assigning to a property is not allowed at this language level.

ar.template: يمكنك إسناد القيم إلى المتغيرات فقط، أما الإسناد إلى الخصائص فغير مسموح به في هذا المستوى من اللغة.

review_flags: Term choice: 'إسناد' for assignment (vs 'تعيين' or the more concrete 'تخزين قيمة في') — confirm for the young-learner age group and lock the choice catalog-wide; first clause adds 'القيم' (values) to make the action concrete for beginners.

'الخصائص' for properties: English singular 'a property' rendered as generic definite plural to parallel 'المتغيرات' (idiomatic Arabic generic reference) — confirm, and confirm 'خاصية' matches the property term used on other Arabic learner-facing surfaces.
Register: the 'أما … فـ' contrast construction is standard school MSA but slightly formal — confirm it suits young learners; simpler fallback is 'لكن الإسناد إلى الخصائص غير مسموح به'.
'في هذا المستوى من اللغة' for 'at this language level' — confirm it matches how JEJ language levels are named elsewhere in the Arabic learner UI.

templates.template_en: '{keyword}' can only be used with '{allowed}' at this language level.

ar.template: لا يمكن استخدام «{keyword}» إلا مع «{allowed}» في هذا المستوى من اللغة.

review_flags: gender-agreement: the masdar construction (لا يمكن استخدام + genitive) deliberately avoids verb/adjective agreement with the interpolated value; confirm it reads naturally with both Arabic pack words (جديد / تاريخ) and raw English tokens (new / Date) in the slots

plural-handling: {allowed} may later carry a list of allowed constructors; 'إلا مع' is number-neutral so the sentence needs no re-keying, but a native reviewer must set the list join (أو vs و, Arabic comma ،) at the render/join layer

register: confirm the exceptive لا يمكن ... إلا reads as warm guidance rather than scolding for young learners; a softer فقط variant was rejected because فقط's scope is ambiguous between 'with {allowed}' and 'at this level'

cross-cluster consistency: 'في هذا المستوى من اللغة' is the fixed rendering of the English tail 'at this language level' — it must match the rendering chosen in every other cluster that carries the same tail

punctuation: Western straight single quotes kept around code-token placeholders and Western full stop kept (stored template stays clean, isolation at render time) — confirm against pack punctuation conventions

templates.template_en: This code could not be read as valid {language}.

ar.template: تعذرت قراءة هذه الشيفرة كشيفرة صالحة بلغة {language}.

review_flags: gender-agreement: no Arabic word inflects against {language} by design — صالحة agrees with the fixed feminine شيفرة, and {language} sits after بلغة in a genitive slot; confirm the sentence stays natural when the value renders in Arabic script (جافاسكريبت) and in Latin script (JavaScript).
register: تعذرت قراءة is standard Arabic UI phrasing but formal; confirm it suits young absolute beginners, or prefer the warmer first-person لم نتمكن من قراءة (apply the same choice cluster-wide).
term-choice: الشيفرة chosen for 'code' over the loanword الكود (target-script policy); confirm age-group familiarity — cluster-wide decision.
style: role-marking كـ in كشيفرة is contested by MSA purists; alternatives بوصفها شيفرة صالحة or على أنها شيفرة صالحة if the reviewer objects.
repetition: شيفرة appears twice (هذه الشيفرة … كشيفرة صالحة); intentional for clarity, reviewer may smooth it.

templates.template_en: This code uses features that are not part of this language level.

ar.template: تستخدم هذه الشيفرة ميزات ليست ضمن هذا المستوى من اللغة.

review_flags: term-choice: ميزات for 'features'; reviewer may prefer خصائص for young learners — pick one and keep it consistent across all clusters.

semantics: هذا المستوى من اللغة must read as the teaching level (JEJ dialect subset) of the programming language, not linguistic register — المستوى اللغوي was deliberately avoided; confirm the intended reading survives for the age group.

plural: ميزات is a fixed, non-interpolated plural taking feminine-singular agreement (ليست) per MSA non-human plural rules; no countable placeholder exists, so later plural-rule work needs no re-keying.
register: confirm cluster consistency with the sibling message (verb-initial frame, same هذه الشيفرة subject, same term for 'code').

templates.template_en: Unexpected '{token}' — check the code just before this point.

ar.template: الرمز «{token}» غير متوقع — تحقق من الشيفرة قبل هذا الموضع مباشرة.

review_flags: Gender agreement: interpolated token is anchored masculine via the category noun 'الرمز' so 'غير متوقع' stays invariant — confirm this reads naturally for every token shape (ASCII punctuation and Arabic pack words alike)
Register: native 'الشيفرة' chosen over loanword 'الكود' — confirm for a young-learner audience; swap to 'الكود' if الشيفرة reads too formal
Category noun 'الرمز' added beyond the bare English 'Unexpected {token}' for grammatical anchoring — confirm the addition is wanted

templates.template_en: A text string was opened but never closed — add the closing quote '{delimiter}'.

ar.template: تم فتح نص ولم يتم إغلاقه — أضف علامة الاقتباس الختامية «{delimiter}».

review_flags: Register: 'تم فتح / لم يتم إغلاقه' software-passive used deliberately because the true passive (فتح / لم يغلق) is ambiguous without diacritics — confirm register for young learners
Terminology: 'علامة الاقتباس' vs 'علامة التنصيص' for quotation mark; also consider unifying to the siblings' plain 'علامة الإغلاق' since the delimiter glyph is shown anyway
'نص' (not 'سلسلة نصية') matches the draft pack's String term — confirm it is clear that a string, not arbitrary prose, is meant

Register: same تم-passive as the other unterminated messages — review once for all three

Grammar: accusative 'عاملا' and dual pronoun 'بينهما' (number + name) — confirm both

placeholders.example: class (back-substitutes to the pack keyword term)

ar.template: «{word}» كلمة محجوزة ولا يمكن استخدامها كاسم.

review_flags: Interpolation: {word} back-substitutes the Arabic pack keyword (e.g. 'ليكن') so the quoted value is itself Arabic — confirm the sentence reads naturally with real pack words and that the feminine agreement chain (كلمة → استخدامها) holds regardless of the word's own gender
Register: 'كاسم' (kaf-as) is contemporary technical usage; prescriptive MSA prefers 'استخدامها اسما' — confirm house style

templates.template_en: '{name}' is not defined — check the spelling, or declare it before using it.

ar.template: الاسم «{name}» غير معرف — تحقق من الإملاء، أو عرفه قبل استخدامه.

review_flags: Gender agreement: the masculine head noun الاسم anchors all agreeing forms (غير معرف، عرفه، استخدامه) so any interpolated identifier stays grammatical — verify it still reads naturally when {name} is a feminine Arabic identifier such as 'القيمة', and that the anchored pattern does not feel bureaucratic.

'غير معرف' intentionally echoes the draft pack's undefined = غير_معرف and the fix verb عرفه (shared root ع-ر-ف): confirm beginners will not conflate this not-declared error with the undefined VALUE; if the conflation is a concern, propose لم يتم تعريفه for the error instead.
Confirm الإملاء is the natural school word for 'spelling' across regions for young learners (alternative: التهجئة).

Quote style: ASCII '…' kept around {name} to match the English family; confirm the pack-wide preference (e.g., «…» guillemets) — no bidi controls are stored, isolation happens at render time per the ratified policy.
Register: direct imperatives تحقق / عرفه address the learner; confirm this lands warm rather than curt in MSA for young learners.

templates.template_en: '{name}' was used before it was given its value — move the declaration above this line.

ar.template: تم استخدام الاسم «{name}» قبل أن يأخذ قيمته — انقل سطر التعريف فوق هذا السطر.

review_flags: Gender agreement: الاسم anchors يأخذ قيمته (masculine) regardless of the interpolated identifier — verify naturalness when {name} is a feminine Arabic identifier.

تم استخدام was chosen over the bare passive استخدم, which without diacritics can misread as the imperative 'use'; confirm the تم construction is acceptable register here, or supply the diacritized passive اسـتُخدم if the pack later allows selective diacritics.

قبل أن يأخذ قيمته renders 'before it was given its value': confirm naturalness for beginners versus alternatives (قبل أن يحصل على قيمته، or the more technical قبل أن تسند إليه قيمة — likely too formal for this register).

سطر التعريف = 'the declaration (line)': confirm تعريف over إعلان as the standing beginner term for variable declaration, consistent with عرفه in jej.name_not_defined and with the pack's ليكن / ثابت pedagogy.

فوق هذا السطر mirrors the visual English 'above this line'; confirm versus the execution-order phrasing إلى ما قبل هذا السطر, whichever native reviewers find clearer for children reading their own code.
Quote style: same ASCII '…' question as the rest of the cluster.

templates.template_en: Cannot read '{member}' because the value is '{literal}' — there is nothing to read from.

placeholders.example: length → طول (back-substitutes to the pack member term)

placeholders.name: literal
placeholders.example: null → عدم or undefined → غير_معرف (back-substitutes to the pack keyword/builtin term)

ar.template: لا يمكن قراءة «{member}» لأن القيمة هي «{literal}» — لا يوجد شيء يمكن القراءة منه.

review_flags: gender: هي agrees with القيمة (fem head noun) and treats the interpolated '{literal}' (عدم / غير_معرف) as a quoted mention — confirm no agreement shift is needed with either builtin term
register: impersonal tail لا يوجد شيء يمكن القراءة منه — confirm it reads naturally for young learners; warmer alternative: فلا يوجد ما يمكن قراءته
punctuation: straight ASCII quotes around placeholders kept to match the cluster/render convention — catalog-wide decision on Arabic guillemets «…» still pending
structure: em-dash problem—explanation shape mirrored from English — confirm dash is acceptable MSA punctuation for learner UI or should become a comma + فـ

templates.template_en: '{callee}' is not a function — check that it holds a function before calling it.

placeholders.name: callee
placeholders.example: score (learner-chosen identifier; may itself be an Arabic word, e.g. نتيجة)

ar.template: الاسم «{callee}» ليس دالة — تأكد من أنه يحمل دالة قبل استدعائه.

review_flags: gender: '{callee}' is predicated masculine (ليس / أنه / استدعائه) using the mentioned-identifier default; learner identifiers may be feminine Arabic nouns (e.g. نتيجة) — confirm the masc-default convention or restructure with a head noun (القيمة '{callee}' ليست دالة …)
terminology: دالة for 'function' is standard MSA math/CS usage; the draft pack has no function term (not in the JEJ surface) — confirm register for young learners
idiom: يحمل ('holds') for a name holding a value — confirm the metaphor reads naturally; alternative يحتوي على
register: imperative تأكد addresses the learner directly (matches English 'check') — confirm warm-imperative is the desired voice for this catalog
Anchor added post-verify: الاسم heads the agreement chain (ليس/أنه/استدعائه) so learner-chosen feminine identifiers do not break agreement.

templates.template_en: '{name}' was declared with '{keyword}' and cannot be given a new value.

placeholders.name: name
placeholders.example: limit (learner-chosen identifier; may itself be an Arabic word, e.g. حد)

placeholders.name: keyword
placeholders.example: const → ثابت (back-substitutes to the pack keyword term)

ar.template: تم تعريف الاسم «{name}» باستخدام «{keyword}»، لذا لا يمكن إعطاؤه قيمة جديدة.

review_flags: register: تم تعريف chosen over bare عرف (ambiguous without diacritics: 'knew' vs 'declared') — confirm the تم-construction is acceptable for learner register or prefer an active form addressing the learner (عرفت '{name}' …)
gender: إعطاؤه masculine pronoun for '{name}' — same masc-default mention decision as jej.not_callable; native reviewer should ratify once, cluster-wide
connector: لذا makes the consequence explicit where English has 'and' — intentional for beginners; confirm
keyword slot: renders as باستخدام 'ثابت' after back-substitution — confirm flow with the pack term interpolated; alternative phrasing بالكلمة '{keyword}'
Anchor added post-verify: الاسم heads the agreement chain (إعطاؤه), matching cluster siblings.

templates.template_en: A loop repeated more than {limit} times and was stopped — check its ending condition.

ar.template: تكررت حلقة أكثر من {limit} مرة فتم إيقافها — تحقق من شرط توقفها.

review_flags: PLURAL: counted noun 'مرة' after {limit} is correct for the typical large limits (11–99 and multiples of 100/1000, e.g. 10000) but values 3–10 require 'مرات'; sentence is structured so only the noun slot changes when CLDR plural categories are wired in — no re-key needed.
GENDER/REGISTER: masculine singular imperative 'تحقق' used as the conventional neutral learner address — confirm this register suits young learners (alternative: softer 'تأكد من').
NATURALNESS: indefinite subject 'تكررت حلقة' chosen over 'إحدى الحلقات' (presupposes multiple loops) and 'هناك حلقة' (filler) — confirm which reads most natural to a native ear.
TERM: 'شرط توقفها' for 'ending condition' — confirm against the standard Arabic CS-pedagogy term (شرط التوقف) used in target curricula.

templates.template_en: '{value}' is not a valid count — use a whole number that is zero or more.

ar.template: القيمة «{value}» غير صالحة كعدد مرات — استخدم عددا صحيحا يساوي صفرا أو أكثر.

review_flags: GENDER: agreement is deliberately anchored to the feminine head noun 'القيمة' preceding the placeholder, so 'غير صالحة' never agrees with the interpolated {value} — confirm the pattern holds when {value} renders as Latin/code text.
REGISTER: 'كعدد مرات' uses modern kaf-as-'in the capacity of'; purist MSA may prefer a rephrase (e.g. 'لا تصلح عددا للمرات') — confirm acceptable for the pack's register.

PHRASING: 'عددا صحيحا يساوي صفرا أو أكثر' for 'a whole number that is zero or more' — confirm for young learners; alternative 'عددا صحيحا موجبا أو صفرا'. Note 'عدد صحيح' is the school math term for integer.

RTL/RENDER: ASCII single quotes surround '{value}' in RTL text; stored template is clean per the bidi policy (isolation at render time) — native reviewer should eyeball the rendered output for quote placement around the interpolated value.

templates.template_en: Too many function calls were waiting at once — a function may be calling itself without an end.

ar.template: تراكمت استدعاءات كثيرة جدا للدوال في وقت واحد — ربما هناك دالة تستدعي نفسها بلا توقف.

review_flags: TERM: 'دالة' for 'function' is the MSA/most-common CS-pedagogy choice, but regional curricula vary (تابع in Syria, اقتران in Jordan) — confirm for the target audience.

SEMANTICS: 'تراكمت' ('piled up') renders 'were waiting at once' by mechanism rather than literally — confirm the accumulation image is acceptable (it is truer to the call stack and clearer for beginners than a literal 'waiting').
PHRASING: 'ربما هناك دالة تستدعي نفسها' chosen over tighter 'ربما تستدعي دالة نفسها' to prevent a beginner misparsing 'تستدعي' as 2nd person ('you call') — confirm the existential reads naturally.
TERM: 'بلا توقف' for 'without an end' — deliberately echoes the توقف word-family from the loop message; confirm, or consider 'دون شرط توقف' to teach the base-case concept explicitly.

templates.template_en: The program ran for more than {seconds} seconds and was stopped.

ar.template: استمر البرنامج في العمل لأكثر من {seconds} من الثواني، لذلك تم إيقافه.

review_flags: PLURAL: {seconds} is countable; the counted noun is kept singular and immediately adjacent ({seconds} ثانية) so CLDR plural categories (ثانية واحدة / ثانيتين / ثوانٍ / ثانية) can be added later without re-keying. Confirm «لأكثر من {seconds} ثانية» is acceptable UI Arabic for 3–10 values, where ثوان is classically required.

REGISTER: تم إيقافه chosen over internal passive أوقف because the passive is ambiguous without diacritics; confirm the تم-construction matches the desired learner register (some style guides prefer the passive verb form).
TONE: لذلك ('therefore') is an intentional beginner-friendly explicitation of the neutral English 'and' — it tells the learner the long run is WHY it was stopped; confirm.
DIGITS: the numeral interpolated into {seconds} sits inside Arabic text; Western vs Eastern Arabic digit choice is a render-time locale decision — confirm the expectation for young Arabic readers.

templates.template_en: The run was cancelled before it finished.

ar.template: تم إلغاء تشغيل البرنامج قبل أن ينتهي.

review_flags: EXPLICITATION: English 'The run' is rendered as تشغيل البرنامج ('the program's run') — bare التشغيل reads dangling for a young learner; confirm the added البرنامج.
REGISTER: تم إلغاء kept parallel to تم إيقافه for cluster consistency; reviewer may prefer أُلغي, which would need a diacritic to disambiguate — hence avoided in the diacritic-free template.
GRAMMAR (low risk): subject of ينتهي is التشغيل (masculine) — internal agreement only, no interpolated value involved.

templates.template_en: A '{error_type}' occurred: {message}

placeholders.name: error_type
placeholders.example: RangeError (rendered as a display term from the CORE-1379 error-type catalog)

placeholders.name: message
placeholders.example: raw engine message pass-through (untranslated by design; fallback only)

ar.template: حدث خطأ من نوع «{error_type}»: {message}

review_flags: GENDER: the frame حدث خطأ من نوع locks verb agreement to the fixed masculine خطأ, so the interpolated {error_type} display term never controls agreement regardless of its gender/number. Verify the frame reads naturally with real CORE-1379 Arabic display terms, and that a term like خطأ المدى does not grate as «خطأ من نوع 'خطأ المدى'» (mild double-خطأ redundancy).

HOMONYM: خطأ ('error') coexists with the draft pack's false → خطأ (the established صحيح/خطأ convention in Arabic CS education). Native reviewer + CORE-1379 catalog author should jointly confirm this overload is acceptable for young learners; the alternative مشكلة was rejected to keep the universal حدث خطأ idiom and stay consistent with catalog term naming.
QUOTES: ASCII straight quotes around {error_type} mirror the English template family and help delimit a possibly-Latin term in RTL context; reviewer may prefer Arabic «» guillemets.

BIDI/PUNCTUATION: {message} is raw untranslated engine text (usually English/LTR) ending an RTL sentence; isolation happens at render time per the ratified policy (stored template is control-free). Confirm the colon + trailing LTR run reads acceptably. No trailing period added, matching English, since the pass-through may carry its own punctuation.
